zone: Master bathroom washing niche and shower
question: (1) Provide the measured niche width/depth and final washer cut sheet. Confirm loaded weight, feet and door clearances, and inlet/drain head. Design a restrained, vibration-resistant support (frame or slab, not a loose marble slab) with anti-walk brackets and a marble finished top at 610 mm; decide whether a leak tray with waste is wanted. (2) Confirm the standpipe/trap position behind the platform (about 112 mm gap, about 229 mm above the machine base): anti-siphon/air-gap detail, an access hatch for rodding, and the architect's niche floor drain (plan about x 4.27, z 33.3 ft, under the platform). Confirm the inlet angle valve and IP-rated RCD socket above the machine top on opposite niche walls. (3) Shower drain, user decision 27 Oct 2026: linear drain along the BACK wall under the mixer, not at the entry. The architect plan shows the shower floor drain at about x 1.27 ft, z 26.37 ft (read from a raster, about ±30 mm); the channel passes over it and the outlet stays under it, about 75 mm toward the wall. Confirm against the actual sleeve and sunken-slab depth; floor falls (about 1:80–1:100) run AWAY from the open front; waterproofing must turn up behind the channel's wall flange and stay continuous at the glass floor channels; flush grate and border, wet-slip rating for the octagon floor and grate. (4) User decision 27 Oct 2026: 25 L vertical geyser high in the north-west corner of the door wall above the vanity. Confirm the selected model's dimensions, weight full and connection side; the wall behind it backs onto the master-bedroom wardrobe end and a block of unknown type on the plan, so confirm wall construction and a fixing rated for the full tank; 143 mm ceiling gap for lifting/service; PRV discharge via the wall chase to a tundish into the vanity basin waste; insulated concealed hot line about 3 m to the shower mixer; dedicated circuit, isolator outside the bathroom, IP rating of the high-level outlet. (5) Glass supplier's fixing detail for two arched fluted returns (stabiliser if required; smooth face to the wet side for hard-water cleaning). The rev 4 towel rail is through-glass on the dry face of the vanity-side return: holes must be cut before toughening. (6) Shower downlight sits inside the enclosure: IP65 fitting on an RCD circuit (with RFI-005). (7) For the 60+ users: blocking or anchor plates behind tile for a vertical grab bar beside the mixer, a fold-down seat on the shower back wall (south end) and a fold-up grab bar on the back wall beside the WC (W9 sill at about 440 mm rules out the side wall). (8) Finishes and storage confirmed by the user 27 Oct 2026; site checks still needed: Master WC shallow sage upper cupboard (about 168 mm deep, 2,035–2,751 mm high; moisture-resistant, termite-treated board, sealed edges, wall fixing), brass WC flush plate and health faucet, tiled cistern enclosure, and the floating vanity (much less storage than the approved floor-standing cabinet). (9) East wall is shared with the living hall and carries the towel bar, hooks and washer valve: confirm construction, fixings and waterproofing. W9/exhaust interplay stays under RFI-006.
owner: Architect/site supervisor, structural professional where required, appliance vendor, plumber, waterproofing applicator, licensed electrician, glass supplier, carpenter
reason: The user requested a 610 mm elevated washer and a reference-style shower; independent QA on rev 3 found unconfirmed services, fixings and finishes. Existing drawings do not specify the washer load or support, service routes, drain outlet, hot-water source, glass fixing or blocking, so these elements of the 3D draft are conceptual and fabrication is blocked.
